ImageDescription.value:
New Ḍōgarā Varnamala in Noto Serif font (Regular). This chart is divided into:
10 vowels (𑠩𑠹𑠦𑠤) - 𑠀 𑠁 𑠂 𑠃 𑠄 𑠅 𑠆 𑠇 𑠈 𑠉,
34 consonants (𑠦𑠹𑠣𑠓𑠹𑠑𑠝) - 𑠊 𑠋 𑠌 𑠍 𑠎 𑠏 𑠐 𑠑 𑠒 𑠓 𑠔 𑠕 𑠖 𑠗 𑠘 𑠙 𑠚 𑠛 𑠜 𑠝 𑠞 𑠟 𑠠 𑠡 𑠢 𑠣 𑠤 𑠥 𑠦 𑠧 𑠨 𑠩 𑠪 𑠫 ,
9 Vowel diacritics (𑠢𑠬𑠙𑠹𑠤𑠬) - 𑠬 (𑠁-𑠢𑠬𑠙𑠹𑠤𑠬), 𑠭 (𑠂-𑠢𑠬𑠙𑠹𑠤𑠬), 𑠮 (𑠃-𑠢𑠬𑠙𑠹𑠤𑠬), 𑠯 (𑠄-𑠢𑠬𑠙𑠹𑠤𑠬), 𑠰 (𑠅-𑠢𑠬𑠙𑠹𑠤𑠬), 𑠳 (𑠆-𑠢𑠬𑠙𑠹𑠤𑠬), 𑠴 (𑠇-𑠢𑠬𑠙𑠹𑠤𑠬), 𑠵 (𑠈-𑠢𑠬𑠙𑠹𑠤𑠬), 𑠶 (𑠉-𑠢𑠬𑠙𑠹𑠤𑠬),
6 Sanskrit origin marks (first three with base letter "𑠀") - 𑠀𑠷 (𑠀𑠝𑠯𑠩𑠹𑠦𑠬𑠤), 𑠀𑠸 (𑠦𑠭𑠩𑠤𑠹𑠌), 𑠀ँ (𑠏𑠝𑠹𑠛𑠹𑠤𑠠𑠭𑠝𑠹𑠛𑠯), 𑠱 (𑠤𑠱-𑠢𑠬𑠙𑠹𑠤𑠬), 𑠲 (𑠤 𑠲-𑠢𑠬𑠙𑠹𑠤𑠬), 𑇁 (𑠀𑠦𑠌𑠹𑠤𑠪),
Vowel-killer mark with base letter "𑠐" - 𑠐𑠹 (𑠦𑠭𑠤𑠬𑠢),
Consonant modifier with base letter "𑠐"- 𑠐𑠺 (𑠝𑠯𑠊𑠺𑠹𑠙𑠬),
4 Punctuation marks - । ॥ - 𑠻
Note 1: Ḍōgarā was standardized in the 1800's by Maharaja Ranbir Singh of Jammu. Old Ḍōgarā was a variant of Tākri used in Jammu. The revised script used Devanāgarī-influenced diacritics and independent letters for easier comprehension.
Note 2: Ḍōgarā has been completely replaced by Devanāgarī as the script for Dogri in everyday life. However, efforts for revival continue.
Note 3: Variant letters for - 𑠑𑠹𑠓 𑠅 𑠜 𑠕 𑠫 𑠂 𑠆 𑠉 𑠌 𑠒 𑠤 𑠜 𑠍 𑠚 𑠎 𑠎 𑠚 𑠘 𑠓 𑠧 𑠠, exist and are found in old manuscripts.
